column4: The national team wins the World Cup. Millions celebrate at the Obelisk and across the country; for a few weeks nobody talks about inflation.
The worst drought in sixty years wipes out the harvest. Billions of dollars in exports are lost.
Extraordinary rains burst rivers and streams. Thousands evacuated and whole neighbourhoods under water.
A grid failure leaves millions without power in the middle of a heatwave. Residents block streets with bonfires.
For the first time since his election, the Argentine Pope tours the country. Huge crowds and a message about poverty no one can ignore.
A newspaper investigation exposes bribes in public works. A driver's notebooks record every bag of cash.
An international miner announces a record investment in a salt flat in the Puna.
With the country cheap in dollars, tourists arrive from all over the world. Bariloche, Iguazú and Buenos Aires are packed.
With prices soaring, crowds loot supermarkets in Greater Buenos Aires, Rosario and Córdoba.
Hundreds of thousands of students, lecturers and families march in defence of public universities. It is one of the largest protests in decades.

column3: An Argentine film wins the Oscar
column4: Argentine cinema wins the award for best international feature once again.
Fire spreads through native forests in the Andes. Firefighters from across the country battle the flames.
The trade surplus breaks records: more dollars come in than in any year in history.
A train with failed brakes crashes into a terminal station. Years of poor maintenance are exposed.
Heads of state from around the world arrive in Buenos Aires for a G20 summit.
The President promotes a cryptocurrency on social media that crashes minutes later. Thousands of investors lose their savings and the opposition calls for impeachment.
Recordings leak of a former official describing a bribery scheme in the purchase of medicines for disabled people.
A batch of contaminated fentanyl causes dozens of deaths in hospitals. Controls on the laboratory are found to have failed.

column3: Devastating storm in a southern Buenos Aires city
column4: Historic rainfall floods a port city within hours: there are deaths, thousands evacuated and entire neighbourhoods destroyed.
The first Latin American Pope dies in Rome. The country declares national mourning and millions bid farewell to the man who made the poor his cause.
Washington announces a 20 billion dollar swap line and buys pesos in the market to halt a run before the elections.
The country suffers the worst dengue epidemic in its history: overwhelmed emergency rooms, repellent shortages and a row over the vaccine.
Extreme cold sends demand soaring: gas is cut to factories and CNG filling stations while LNG cargoes are rushed in.
Air traffic controllers strike over pay: hundreds of flights cancelled over a long weekend.
After years of drug violence, murders in Rosario fall to a two-decade low thanks to the federal operation.
An international agency upgrades Argentina's sovereign rating. Country risk breaks through a new low.
A historic factory on the outskirts of Buenos Aires closes, leaving hundreds out of work. The workers camp at the gate.
Tanks cross a border in Eastern Europe. Grain and energy markets go wild.

column3: The Strait of Hormuz is closed
column4: War in the Gulf blocks a fifth of the world's oil. Brent tops 120 dollars; Asian refineries ask for Argentine crude.
Washington announces tariffs on the whole world and China retaliates. Argentine steel and aluminium are hit.
The Federal Reserve raises its rate for the first time in years. Argentine bonds fall and country risk rebounds.
The real collapses and Brazil enters recession. Argentine car plants suspend shifts.
A poor US harvest and Chinese demand push soybeans to a ten-year high.
A new respiratory virus spreads across every continent. Borders close.
World stock markets fall 20% in a week. Funds go bust and credit freezes.
A new crisis in Venezuela pushes thousands of families south. Many reach Buenos Aires.
The European Parliament ratifies the Mercosur agreement. Beef, wine and lemon producers celebrate; industry worries.
Beijing closes its largest purchase of Argentine soybeans in years amid its trade war with the US.
